Next year marks the 20th anniversary of the iPhone's launch, and reports suggest the iPhone Pro models will receive a completely refreshed design. The latest leaked information has also revealed the specific specifications of the reportedly larger screen sizes.

Next year's iPhone Pro models will feature larger 6.4-inch and 7-inch displays

In 2017, to celebrate the 10th anniversary of the iPhone, Apple specially launched a particularly meaningful model: the iPhone X.

There are rumours that the company is preparing an equally distinctive product for next year's 20th anniversary.

According to reports, next year's iPhone Pro models will adopt a full-screen design with four-sided curved edges, with the display extending to the edges of the device.

The Dynamic Island cutout may be shrunk, or even completely removed, giving the entire device a seamless, all-glass, one-piece appearance.

According to the latest post by tipster Digital Chat Station, Apple is also preparing new screen sizes. He pointed out that the company is testing the following specifications:

  • iPhone Pro: 6.4 inches, up from the current 6.3 inches
  • iPhone Pro Max: 7 inches, up from the current 6.9 inches

He added that the overall device dimensions of both models will increase, but they will maintain the same screen aspect ratio as the existing models. This means the larger screen is not simply due to narrower bezels.

Apple last increased the screen sizes of its Pro models in 2024, when the iPhone 16 Pro went from 6.1 inches to 6.3 inches, and the Pro Max went from 6.7 inches to 6.9 inches.

Although the increase seems modest on paper, combined with the four-sided curved design, it should deliver a more refreshed feel and overall visual experience.

What are your thoughts on the rumoured design of next year's iPhone Pro models? Feel free to share your opinions in the comments section.
